title.zh: 卷四十九 吳書四 劉繇太史慈士燮傳
title.en: Volume 49: Book of Wu 4 - Biographies of Liu Yao, Taishi Ci, and Shi Xie
title.raw: 卷四十九 吳書四 劉繇太史慈士燮傳 Volume 49: Book of Wu 4 - Biographies of Liu Yao, Taishi Ci, and Shi Xie

sentences.zh: 劉繇，字正禮，東萊牟平人也。

translations.literal: Liu Yao, courtesy name Zhengli, was a native of Mouping in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, styled Zhengli, came from Mouping in Donglai commandery.

sentences.zh: 齊孝王少子封牟平侯，子孫家焉。

translations.literal: The youngest son of Prince Xiao of Qi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Mouping, and his descendants made their home there.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son of Prince Xiao of Qi had been enfeoffed as Marquis of Mouping, and his descendants settled there.

sentences.zh: 繇伯父寵，為漢太尉。

translations.literal: Yao's uncle Liu Chong served as Grand Commandant of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's uncle Liu Chong held the Han office of Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 〈续汉书曰：繇祖父本，师受经传，博学群书，号为通儒。

translations.literal: The Continued Book of Han states: Yao's grandfather Ben studied the Classics under a teacher, was broadly learned in many texts, and was called a thoroughly versed scholar.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Continued Book of Han, Yao's grandfather Liu Ben took instruction in the Classics and histories, read widely, and was known as a Confucian master of comprehensive learning.

sentences.zh: 举贤良方正，为般长，卒官。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Worthy and Incorrupt and appointed chief of Pan district; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as worthy and upright, he served as chief of Pan district and died while holding that post.

sentences.zh: 宠字祖荣，受父业，以经明行修，举孝廉，光禄

translations.literal: Chong's courtesy name was Zurong; he inherited his father's learning. Because his mastery of the Classics was clear and his conduct cultivated, he was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, Guangluxun
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong, styled Zurong, continued his father's scholarship; honored for classical learning and upright conduct, he earned recommendation as filial and incorrupt and entered the Guangluxun cadre

sentences.zh: （大夫）

translations.literal: (Grandee)
translations.idiomatic: (completing the compound title: Supervising Secretary under the Masters of Writing)

sentences.zh: 察四行，除东平陵令。

translations.literal: He was examined on the Four Conducts and appointed magistrate of Dongpingling.
translations.idiomatic: After evaluation of the four virtues of conduct, he was appointed magistrate of Dongpingling.

sentences.zh: 视事数年，以母病弃官，百姓士民攀舆拒轮，充塞道路，车不得前，乃止亭，轻服潜遁，归脩供养。

translations.literal: After several years in office, because his mother fell ill he resigned his post; commoners and gentry dragged at his carriage and blocked the wheels, filling the roads so the cart could not advance; he therefore halted at a post station, changed into plain clothes, and slipped away in secret to return home and provide for her.
translations.idiomatic: After a few years in office he resigned to nurse his ailing mother; townspeople clung to his carriage until the roads were impassable. He halted at a relay station, changed into humble clothes, and vanished quietly homeward to devote himself to her care.

sentences.zh: 后辟大将军府，稍迁会稽太守，正身率下，郡中大治。

translations.literal: Later he was summoned to the Grand General's office and gradually rose to Grand Administrator of Kuaiji; he corrected himself and led those below him, and the commandery was greatly well governed.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to staff the Grand General's headquarters, he rose step by step to Grand Administrator of Kuaiji, where personal rectitude set the tone and good order prevailed.

sentences.zh: 徵入为将作大匠。

translations.literal: He was summoned to court as Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: The court recalled him as Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 山阴县民去治数十里有若邪中在山谷间，五六老翁年皆七八十，闻宠迁，相率共送宠，人赍百钱。

translations.literal: The people of Shanyin district lived several dozen li from the seat of government in Ruoye amid mountain valleys; five or six old men, all seventy or eighty years old, hearing that Chong was transferred, went together to see him off, each carrying a hundred cash.
translations.idiomatic: In Shanyin, settlements lay dozens of li from the capital in the Ruoye valleys—five or six men in their seventies and eighties who heard Liu Chong was leaving banded together to send him off, each bearing a hundred coins.

sentences.zh: 宠见，劳来曰：“父老何乃自苦远来！

translations.literal: When Chong saw them, he consoled them and said, "Why have you elders troubled yourselves to come so far!
translations.idiomatic: Seeing them, Chong urged them to spare themselves: "Why should you elders wear yourselves out with such a journey!

sentences.zh: ”皆对曰：“山谷鄙老，生未尝至郡县。

translations.literal: They all replied, "We old rustics in the hills have never in our lives come to the district or prefectural seat.
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "We old hill folk have never once visited the county or commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 他时吏发求不去，民间或夜不绝狗吠，竟夕民不得安。

translations.literal: At other times when officials came collecting taxes we could not drive them off; sometimes dogs barked through the night without cease, and the people could not rest an entire evening.
translations.idiomatic: In other years, when clerks came demanding levies, we could never be rid of them; dogs might yap all night, and we never knew a peaceful dusk.

sentences.zh: 自明府下车以来，狗不夜吠，吏稀至民间，年老遭值圣化，今闻当见弃去，故戮力来送。

translations.literal: Since Your Honor took office, dogs do not bark at night, and clerks rarely come among the people; we old men have encountered sagely rule. Now we hear you are to be cast aside and must leave, so we have strained every nerve to come see you off.
translations.idiomatic: Since you arrived, nights are free of barking dogs and clerks seldom trouble our homes; we old folk have tasted enlightened government. Learning you are being forced away, we turned out in force to bid you farewell.

sentences.zh: ”宠谢之，为选受一大钱，故会稽号宠为取一钱太守。

translations.literal: Chong thanked them and had each accept one large coin; therefore Kuaiji nicknamed Chong the Grand Administrator who took one coin.
translations.idiomatic: Chong thanked them and arranged for each to accept but one large copper coin—hence Kuaiji dubbed him "the grand administrator who took a single coin."

sentences.zh: 其清如是。

translations.literal: His integrity was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his austerity.

sentences.zh: 宠前后历二郡，八居九列，四登三事。

translations.literal: Chong successively served two commanderies, eight times held posts among the Nine Ministers, and four times ascended to the Three Ducal Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chong governed two commanderies in succession, rose eight times into the Nine Ministers' ranks, and four times reached the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 家不藏贿，无重宝器，恆菲饮食，薄衣服，弊车羸马，号为窭陋。

translations.literal: His household hoarded no bribes, possessed no precious vessels, constantly ate plain food, wore thin clothing, used broken-down carts and feeble horses, and was known as destitute and shabby.
translations.idiomatic: He kept no illicit wealth, owned no costly treasures, ate simply, dressed plainly, and rode in ramshackle wagons with worn-out horses—people called his household threadbare.

sentences.zh: 三去相位，辄归本土。

translations.literal: Three times he left the chancellor's seat and always returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he stepped down from chief ministership and each time returned to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 往来京师，常下道脱骖过，人莫知焉。

translations.literal: Traveling to and from the capital, he habitually left the main road, unhitched a trace horse, and passed by; no one recognized him.
translations.idiomatic: On journeys to and from the capital he routinely slipped off the highway, unhitched a side horse, and rode past unrecognized.

sentences.zh: 宠尝欲止亭，亭吏止之曰：“整顿传舍，以待刘公，不可得止。

translations.literal: Chong once wished to stop at a post station; the station clerk stopped him, saying, "We are putting the relay lodge in order to await Lord Liu; you may not stop here.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Chong meant to halt at a courier station, but the attendant barred him: "We are preparing the lodge for Minister Liu—you cannot stay.

sentences.zh: ”宠因过去。

translations.literal: Chong therefore passed on.
translations.idiomatic: Chong accordingly rode on.

sentences.zh: 其廉俭皆此类也。

translations.literal: His incorruption and frugality were all of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His integrity and thrift ran in this vein throughout.

sentences.zh: 以老病卒于家。〉

translations.literal: He died of old age and illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his days at home, worn down by age and sickness.

sentences.zh: 繇兄岱，字公山，歷位侍中，兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Yao's elder brother Dai, courtesy name Gongshan, successively held the posts of Palace Attendant and Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Liu Dai, styled Gongshan, served in turn as Palace Attendant and Inspector of Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 〈续汉书曰：繇父舆，一名方，山阳太守。

translations.literal: The Continued Book of Han states: Yao's father Yu, also named Fang, was Grand Administrator of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Continued Book of Han records Yao's father Liu Yu—also called Fang—as Grand Administrator of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 岱、繇皆有隽才。

translations.literal: Dai and Yao both possessed outstanding talent.
translations.idiomatic: Both Dai and Yao were men of remarkable ability.

sentences.zh: 《英雄记》称岱孝悌仁恕，以虚己受人。〉

translations.literal: The Record of Heroes states that Dai was filial, fraternal, humane, and forgiving, and with empty-minded modesty accepted others.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Heroes praises Dai for filial devotion, kindness, and tolerance, and for receiving others with humble openness.

sentences.zh: 繇年十九，從父韙為賊所劫質。

translations.literal: When Yao was nineteen, his father's elder brother Wei was seized by bandits as a hostage.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen, Yao saw his uncle Wei taken hostage by bandits.

sentences.zh: 繇篡取以歸，由是顯名。

translations.literal: Yao snatched him away and brought him home; by this he became famous.
translations.idiomatic: He wrested his uncle free and brought him home—a deed that made his name.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為郎中，除下邑長。

translations.literal: He was recommended as Filial and Incorrupt and appointed Gentleman of the Palace; he was assigned magistrate of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he became a Gentleman of the Palace and was named magistrate of Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 時郡守以貴戚托之，遂棄官去。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Administrator, relying on noble connections, leaned on him for favors, so he abandoned his post and left.
translations.idiomatic: The grand administrator, a man of influential kin, tried to trade on Yao's office; Yao resigned and walked away.

sentences.zh: 州辟部濟南，濟南相中常侍子，貪穢不循，繇奏免之。

translations.literal: The province summoned him to serve on the staff of Jinan; the Jinan chancellor was the son of a Regular Palace Attendant, greedy and corrupt and not following regulations; Yao memorialized and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial inspector called him to Jinan's staff; the commandery chancellor there was a palace eunuch's son—venal and lawless—so Yao impeached him and secured his removal.

sentences.zh: 平原陶丘洪薦繇，欲令舉茂才。

translations.literal: Tao Qiuhong of Pingyuan recommended Yao and wished to have him nominated as Outstanding Talent.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qiuhong of Pingyuan urged Yao's nomination as Outstanding Talent.

sentences.zh: 刺吏曰：「前年舉公山。

translations.literal: The Inspector said, "The year before last I nominated Gongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector replied, "I already nominated Gongshan two years ago.

sentences.zh: 奈何復舉正禮乎？

translations.literal: How could I nominate Zhengli again?
translations.idiomatic: How can I elevate Zhengli as well?

sentences.zh: 」洪曰：「若明使君用公山於前，擢正禮於後，所謂御二龍於長塗，騁騏驥於千里，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Hong said, "If the enlightened envoy employs Gongshan first and promotes Zhengli afterward, that is what they call driving two dragons along a long road and galloping fine horses for a thousand li—is it not fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Hong said, "If you advance Gongshan first and lift Zhengli next, you harness two dragons on the long road and let twin steeds run a thousand li—what could be better!

sentences.zh: 」會辟司空掾，除侍御史，不就。

translations.literal: Just then he was summoned as an aide to the Minister of Works and appointed Palace Assistant Clerk; he did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: He was then summoned as aide to the Minister of Works and offered the post of Palace Assistant Clerk, which he declined.

sentences.zh: 避亂淮浦，詔書以為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Fleeing turmoil he went to Huaipu; an imperial edict appointed him Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He took refuge at Huaipu amid the chaos; an edict named him Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 時袁術在淮南，繇畏憚，不敢之州。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Shu was in Huainan; Yao feared him and did not dare go to the province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu held Huainan, and Yao, wary of him, hesitated to enter his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 欲南渡江，吳景，孫賁迎置曲阿。

translations.literal: Wishing to cross south of the Yangzi, Wu Jing and Sun Ben welcomed him and installed him at Qu'e.
translations.idiomatic: Planning to cross the river southward, he was received by Wu Jing and Sun Ben, who settled him at Qu'e.

sentences.zh: 術圖為僭逆，攻沒諸郡縣。

translations.literal: Shu plotted usurpation and attacked and overran the various commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu aimed at rebellion, overrunning commanderies and counties.

sentences.zh: 繇遣樊能、張英屯江邊以拒之。

translations.literal: Yao sent Fan Neng and Zhang Ying to camp along the riverbank to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao stationed Fan Neng and Zhang Ying along the river to hold him off.

sentences.zh: 以景、賁術所授用，乃迫逐使去。

translations.literal: Because Jing and Ben were men Shu had commissioned, Yao compelled them to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Because Wu Jing and Sun Ben held appointments from Yuan Shu, Yao drove them out.

sentences.zh: 於是術乃自置揚州刺史，與景、賁並力攻英、能等，歲余不下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu himself appointed Inspector of Yang Province and together with Jing and Ben jointly attacked Ying, Neng, and the others; for more than a year they could not take them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shu then installed his own inspector of Yang Province and joined Jing and Ben in besieging Ying and Neng—yet after a year still could not break them.

sentences.zh: 漢命加繇為牧，振武將軍，眾數萬人。

translations.literal: Han invested Yao as Governor, General Who Shakes Might, with a host of several tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court promoted Yao to governor, General Who Shakes Might, at the head of tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 孫策東渡，破英、能等。

translations.literal: Sun Ce crossed east and defeated Ying, Neng, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce crossed to the east and routed Fan Neng and Zhang Ying.

sentences.zh: 繇奔丹徒，

translations.literal: Yao fled to Dantu
translations.idiomatic: Yao retreated toward Dantu

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《汉纪》曰：刘繇将奔会稽，许子将曰：“会稽富实，策之所贪，且穷在海隅，不可往也。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong's Han Annals states: When Liu Yao was about to flee to Kuaiji, Xu Zijiang said, "Kuaiji is rich and plentiful—Sun Ce covets it—and stranded on the sea's edge it is no place to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's Han Annals records that as Liu Yao prepared to withdraw to Kuaiji, Xu Shao warned him: "Kuaiji is prosperous—exactly what Sun Ce wants—and tucked away at the ocean's rim offers no refuge.

sentences.zh: 不如豫章，北连豫壤，西接荆州。

translations.literal: Better Yuzhang—it joins Yu province on the north and borders Jingzhou on the west.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhang is better: it links northward with the Central Plain and touches Jingzhou on the west.

sentences.zh: 若收合吏民，遣使贡献，与曹兗州相闻，虽有袁公路隔在其间，其人豺狼，不能久也。

translations.literal: If you gather officials and commoners and send envoys with tribute to keep in touch with Governor Cao of Yan Province, although Yuan Gonglu lies between you, he is a wolfish man and cannot last.
translations.idiomatic: Rally officials and people, send tribute, and open channels to Cao Cao in Yan—even with Yuan Shu between you, that predator cannot endure long.

sentences.zh: 足下受王命，孟德、景升必相救济。

translations.literal: You bear the king's commission; Mengde and Jingsheng are certain to aid you.
translations.idiomatic: You carry imperial mandate; Cao Cao and Liu Biao will surely lend relief.

sentences.zh: ”繇从之。〉

translations.literal: Yao followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Yao took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 遂泝江南保豫章，駐彭澤。

translations.literal: He therefore went upstream on the Yangzi southward and held Yuzhang, stationing himself at Pengze.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore moved upriver on the southern shore to secure Yuzhang and camped at Pengze.

sentences.zh: 笮融先至。

translations.literal: Ze Rong arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Rong got there ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 〈笮音壮力反。〉

translations.literal: 〈Phonetic gloss: the surname Ze is read zhuang-li fan (fanqie spelling).〉
translations.idiomatic: Pronunciation note: Ze is given the fanqie reading zhuang-li fan.

sentences.zh: 殺太守朱皓，

translations.literal: He killed Grand Administrator Zhu Hao
translations.idiomatic: He murdered Grand Administrator Zhu Hao

sentences.zh: 〈《献帝春秋》曰：是岁，繇屯彭泽，又使融助皓讨刘表所用太守诸葛玄。

translations.literal: The Annals of Emperor Xian states: That year Yao was stationed at Pengze and also sent Rong to assist Hao in campaigning against Grand Administrator Zhuge Xuan, whom Liu Biao had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Annals of Emperor Xian notes that Yao camped at Pengze and detached Ze Rong to help Zhu Hao against Zhuge Xuan, Liu Biao's appointee as grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 许子将谓繇曰：“笮融出军，不顾

translations.literal: Xu Zijiang said to Yao, "When Ze Rong leads troops out, he disregards
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shao told Yao, "When Ze Rong takes the field he shows no regard for

translations.literal: (missions)
translations.idiomatic: his orders—

sentences.zh: 名义者也。

translations.literal: and what is called duty and reputation."
translations.idiomatic: or for honor and duty."

sentences.zh: 硃文明善推诚以信人，宜使密防之。

translations.literal: Minister Zhu is by nature inclined to trust others with open sincerity; you should secretly guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Hao is trusting by nature; have him watch Ze Rong closely.

sentences.zh: ”融到，果诈杀皓，代领郡事。〉

translations.literal: When Rong arrived, he indeed treacherously killed Hao and seized control of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Rong arrived, murdered Zhu Hao by treachery, and usurped the commandery.

sentences.zh: 入居郡中。

translations.literal: He entered and occupied the commandery seat.
translations.idiomatic: He moved into the administrative center.

sentences.zh: 繇進討融，為融所破，更復招合屬縣，攻破融，融敗走人山。

translations.literal: Yao advanced to attack Rong but was defeated by Rong; he again gathered the subordinate counties, broke Rong, and Rong fled defeated into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Yao marched against Ze Rong but lost; regrouping his counties, he routed Ze Rong, who fled broken into the hills.

sentences.zh: 為民所殺。

translations.literal: He was killed by the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners killed him.

sentences.zh: 繇尋病卒，時年四十二。

translations.literal: Yao soon afterward fell ill and died; he was forty-two years old.
translations.idiomatic: Yao died of illness not long after, at forty-two.

sentences.zh: 笮融者，丹楊人。

translations.literal: Ze Rong was a man of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ze Rong came from Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初聚眾數百，往依徐州牧陶謙。

translations.literal: At first he gathered several hundred followers and went to attach himself to Xu Province Governor Tao Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He first raised a few hundred men and threw in his lot with Tao Qian, governor of Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 謙使督廣陵、彭城運漕，遂放縱擅殺，坐斷三郡委輸以自入。

translations.literal: Qian had him supervise transport between Guangling and Pengcheng; thereupon he wantonly killed at will and monopolized the tribute convoys of three commanderies for his own intake.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Qian put him in charge of grain transport between Guangling and Pengcheng; Ze Rong then slaughtered freely and seized the riverborne revenue of three commanderies for himself.

sentences.zh: 乃大起浮圖祠，以銅為人，黃金塗身，衣以錦采，垂銅槃九重，下為重樓閣道，可容三千餘人。

translations.literal: He greatly raised Buddha halls, casting human images in bronze, gilding them with gold, clothing them in brocades, suspending nine tiers of bronze bowls, and beneath building multi-story galleries and walkways that could hold more than three thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: He erected vast Buddhist shrines: bronze statues gilded with gold, robed in figured silk, hung with nine tiers of bronze bowls, and under them built tiered galleries and elevated walks seating three thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 悉課讀佛經，令界內及旁郡人有好佛者聽受道，復其他役以招致之，由此遠近前後至者五千餘人戶。

translations.literal: He made them all recite Buddhist scriptures; he allowed those within his borders and in neighboring commanderies who favored Buddhism to receive the teaching, exempting other labor duties to attract them; by this means more than five thousand households came from far and near before and after.
translations.idiomatic: He set disciples to chanting sutras, welcomed Buddhists from his territory and beyond by waiving other corvée, and drew more than five thousand households from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 每浴佛，多設酒飯，布席於路，經數十里，民人來觀及就食且萬人，費以巨億計。

translations.literal: Whenever they bathed the Buddha, they set out wine and food in great quantity, spread mats along the road for several tens of li, and common people came to watch and eat—nearly ten thousand at a sitting—costing hundreds of millions in cash.
translations.idiomatic: At each ritual bathing of the Buddha he laid out feasts along miles of roadway; tens of thousands thronged to watch and eat, at a cost reckoned in hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 曹公攻陶謙，徐土騷動，融將男女數萬口，馬三千匹，走廣陵，廣陵太守趙昱待以賓禮。

translations.literal: When Duke Cao attacked Tao Qian, the land of Xu was in turmoil; Rong led several tens of thousands of men and women and three thousand horses and fled to Guangling; Grand Administrator Zhao Yu of Guangling received him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao struck Tao Qian, Xu Province churned; Ze Rong fled toward Guangling with tens of thousands of people and three thousand horses. Zhao Yu, grand administrator of Guangling, welcomed him as an honored guest.

sentences.zh: 先是，彭城相薛禮為陶謙所逼，屯秣陵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Chancellor of Pengcheng Xue Li, pressed by Tao Qian, had encamped at Moling.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Xue Li, chancellor of Pengcheng—harried by Tao Qian—had camped at Moling.

sentences.zh: 融利廣陵之眾，因酒酣殺昱，放兵大略，因載而去。

translations.literal: Rong coveted Guangling's multitude; when drunk at a banquet he killed Yu, let his troops plunder broadly, then loaded up and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Coveting Guangling's manpower, Ze Rong murdered Zhao Yu in his cups, unleashed his men to loot widely, then marched away laden with spoils.

sentences.zh: 過殺禮，然後殺皓。

translations.literal: Passing along he killed Li, then afterward killed Hao.
translations.idiomatic: En route he slew Xue Li, then later murdered Zhu Hao.

sentences.zh: 後策西伐江夏，還過豫章，收載繇喪，善遇其家。

translations.literal: Later Ce campaigned west against Jiangxia; on the return he passed through Yuzhang, collected Yao's coffin for transport, and treated his family kindly.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Ce campaigned west to Jiangxia; on his way back through Yuzhang he took charge of Liu Yao's funeral train and treated his kin with kindness.

sentences.zh: 王朗遺策書曰："劉正禮昔初臨州，未能自達，實賴尊門為之先後。

translations.literal: Wang Lang sent Ce a letter saying, "Liu Zhengli when he first came to the province could not establish himself on his own and truly relied on your house to prepare the way before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lang wrote Sun Ce: "When Liu Zhengli first entered the province he could not stand on his own and indeed leaned on your family to open the way.

sentences.zh: 用能濟江成治，有所處定。

translations.literal: Thus he was able to cross the Yangzi and achieve good government and settle matters.
translations.idiomatic: Only thus could he cross the river, establish rule, and find his footing.

sentences.zh: 踐境之禮，感分結意，情在終始。

translations.literal: The courtesy due one entering your territory moved him and knit friendship; his feeling ran from first to last.
translations.idiomatic: The welcome at your border stirred him and sealed a bond meant to endure.

sentences.zh: 後以袁氏之嫌，稍更乖刺。

translations.literal: Later, because of suspicion involving the Yuans, they gradually grew estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Yuan-clan suspicions drove them slowly apart.

sentences.zh: 更以同盟，還為仇敵，原其本心，實非所樂。

translations.literal: Although they had been allies, they turned into foes; searching the root of his heart, it was truly not what he wished.
translations.idiomatic: Though once allies, they became enemies—yet at heart neither had desired it.

sentences.zh: 康寧之後，常願渝平更成，復踐宿好。

translations.literal: After peace returned, he always wished to clear the slate and restore their former friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Once calm returned he longed to wipe away the breach and renew their old accord.

sentences.zh: 一爾分離，款意不昭，奄然殂隕，可為傷恨。

translations.literal: With one such separation his earnest intent never shone forth; suddenly he perished—how lamentable.
translations.idiomatic: That single rupture left fond intentions unspoken; his sudden death is cause for grief.

sentences.zh: 知敦以厲薄，德以報怨，收骨育孤，哀亡愍存，捐既往之猜。

translations.literal: I know you use generosity to strengthen what is thin, and virtue to repay injury; you gather bones and rear orphans, mourn the dead and pity the living, casting aside past suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: I know you shore up the weak with generosity and answer injury with virtue—gathering his bones, raising his orphans, grieving the dead and cherishing the living, putting old mistrust aside.

sentences.zh: 保六尺之托，誠深恩重分，美名厚實也。

translations.literal: Protecting the charge of six feet of orphanhood is truly deep kindness and heavy obligation—fine reputation and solid substance.
translations.idiomatic: To safeguard a child's lone charge is profound grace and weighty duty—both honorable name and tangible good.

sentences.zh: 昔魯人雖有齊怨，不廢喪紀，《春秋》善之，謂之得禮，誠良史之所宜借，鄉校之所歎聞。

translations.literal: Formerly the people of Lu, though they bore enmity toward Qi, did not abandon mourning observances; the Spring and Autumn Annals praised them, calling it obtaining ritual—what fine historians ought to cite and village schools ought to hear praised.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu, though they hated Qi, still observed mourning rites; the Spring and Autumn Annals approved this as proper ritual—an example historians should borrow and hearths should celebrate.

sentences.zh: 正禮元子，致有志操，想必有以殊異。

translations.literal: Zhengli's eldest son by his principal wife has arrived with resolve and integrity; surely there will be something remarkable about him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengli's eldest son has come forward with evident purpose and principle—no doubt he will prove extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 威盛刑行，施之以恩，不亦優哉!"

translations.literal: Where might is abundant and punishments run their course, to bestow kindness upon him—is that not the highest course!"
translations.idiomatic: When authority is firm and law has done its work, to overlay it with kindness—could anything be finer!"

sentences.zh: 子 基

translations.literal: Son Ji
translations.idiomatic: Son: Ji

sentences.zh: 繇長子基，字敬輿。

translations.literal: Yao's eldest son Ji, courtesy name Jingyu.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Liu Ji, styled Jingyu.

sentences.zh: 年十四，居繇喪盡禮，故吏饋餉，皆無所受。

translations.literal: At fourteen, while observing mourning for Yao he fulfilled every rite; former subordinates brought gifts, and he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he observed his father's mourning with full ritual propriety, refusing every offering from old retainers.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：基遭多难，婴丁困苦，潜处味道，不以为戚。

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: Ji encountered many hardships, suffered bitter want in youth, dwelt in seclusion savoring the Way, and did not take it as sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book says Ji knew repeated calamities and bitter poverty in youth, yet lived quietly cultivating the Way without nursing resentment.

sentences.zh: 与群弟居，常夜卧早起，妻妾希见其面。

translations.literal: Dwelling with his younger brothers, he often slept late and rose early; his wives and concubines seldom saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: Living with his brothers he kept farmer's hours—his wives and concubines rarely glimpsed him.

sentences.zh: 诸弟敬惮，事之犹父。

translations.literal: The younger brothers revered and feared him and served him as they would a father.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers stood in awe of him and served him like a father.

sentences.zh: 不妄交游，门无杂宾。〉

translations.literal: He did not casually socialize; no improper guests crossed his gate.
translations.idiomatic: He formed no idle friendships; no riffraff darkened his door.

sentences.zh: 姿容美好，孫權愛敬之。

translations.literal: His bearing and looks were handsome; Sun Quan loved and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome in face and deportment, he won Sun Quan's affection and esteem.

sentences.zh: 權為驃騎將軍，辟東曹掾，拜輔義校尉、建忠中郎將。

translations.literal: When Quan was General of Agile Cavalry, he summoned Ji as aide to the East Bureau and appointed him Colonel Who Supports Righteousness and General of the Household Who Establishes Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: While holding the title General of Agile Cavalry, Sun Quan called Liu Ji to staff the East Bureau and invested him as Colonel Who Supports Righteousness and General of the Household for Establishing Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 權為吳王，遷基大農。

translations.literal: When Quan became King of Wu, Ji was promoted to Grand Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Quan took the kingship of Wu, Liu Ji rose to Grand Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 權嘗宴飲，騎都尉虞翻醉酒犯忤，權欲殺之，威怒甚盛，由基諫爭，翻以得免。

translations.literal: Once when Quan feasted, Commandant of Cavalry Yu Fan, drunk, gave offense; Quan wished to kill him, and his majestic wrath was very great—because Ji remonstrated earnestly, Fan was spared.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet Yu Fan, drunk, insulted Sun Quan, who in fury meant to execute him; Liu Ji's desperate pleading saved Fan's life.

sentences.zh: 權大暑時，嘗於船中宴飲，於船樓上值雷雨，權以蓋自覆，又命覆基，餘人不得也。

translations.literal: In great summer heat Quan once drank aboard ship; on the ship tower they encountered thunder and rain—Quan covered himself with an umbrella and also ordered Ji covered; the others did not receive this.
translations.idiomatic: On a sweltering day Sun Quan banqueted on a boat; when a storm broke over the deckhouse he sheltered himself with a canopy and had one spread for Liu Ji alone—no one else was so favored.

sentences.zh: 其見待如此。

translations.literal: He was treated thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the regard Sun Quan showed him.

sentences.zh: 徙郎中令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of the Gentlemen of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to the post of Prefect of the Palace Gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 權稱尊號，改為光祿勳，分平尚書事。

translations.literal: When Quan assumed the imperial title, Ji was changed to Superintendent of the Imperial Household and shared oversight of Masters of Writing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Sun Quan's accession Liu Ji became Superintendent of the Imperial Household and jointly supervised secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 年四十九卒。

translations.literal: He died at forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 後權為子霸納基女，賜第一區。

translations.literal: Later Quan took Ji's daughter as wife for his son Ba and granted one estate.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sun Quan married Liu Ji's daughter to his son Sun Ba and presented the family with a landed residence.

sentences.zh: 四時寵賜，與全、張比。

translations.literal: Seasonal favors and gifts ranked alongside those to the Quan and Zhang clans.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial largesse through the seasons matched what the Quan and Zhang families received.

sentences.zh: 基二弟，鑠、尚，皆騎都尉。

translations.literal: Ji had two younger brothers, Shuo and Shang; both were Commandants of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Liu Shuo and Liu Shang both served as Commandants of Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 太史慈

translations.literal: Taishi Ci
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci

sentences.zh: 太史慈字子義，東萊黃人也。

translations.literal: Taishi Ci, courtesy name Ziyi, was a native of Huang in Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci, styled Ziyi, hailed from Huang district in Donglai.

sentences.zh: 少好學，仕郡奏曹史。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning and served the commandery as clerk of the Memorial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was bookish and held the commandery post of clerk for memorials.

sentences.zh: 會郡與州有隙，曲直未分，以先聞者為善。

translations.literal: It happened that the commandery and the province were at odds; right and wrong had not been decided, and whoever got word out first was deemed in the right.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery and provincial authorities were feuding with no verdict yet in sight—the side that lodged its report first would carry the day.

sentences.zh: 時州章已去，郡守恐後之，求可使者。

translations.literal: By then the province's memorial had already been sent; the Grand Administrator, fearing he would lag behind, sought someone who could go.
translations.idiomatic: The province had already dispatched its memorial; the grand administrator, afraid of coming second, looked for a courier.

sentences.zh: 慈年二十一，以選行，晨夜取道，到洛陽，詣公車門，見州吏始欲求通。

translations.literal: Ci was twenty-one; chosen for the mission, he pressed on day and night, reached Luoyang, went to the Gate of the Imperial Coaches, and saw the provincial clerk just about to seek entry.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci, twenty-one, was picked for the run. He rode night and day to Luoyang, reached the Gate of the Imperial Coaches, and arrived as the provincial clerk was preparing to file.

sentences.zh: 慈問曰：「君欲通章邪？

translations.literal: Ci asked, "Do you wish to submit the memorial?
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci asked, "Are you here to submit that memorial?

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「然。

translations.literal: The clerk said, "Yes.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said, "I am.

sentences.zh: 」問：「章安在？

translations.literal: Ci asked, "Where is the memorial?
translations.idiomatic: "Where is it?

sentences.zh: 」曰：「車上。

translations.literal: He replied, "On the cart.
translations.idiomatic: "In the wagon.

sentences.zh: 」慈曰：「章題署得無誤邪？

translations.literal: Ci said, "Could there be an error in the heading and signature? Bring it for me to look at.
translations.idiomatic: "Is the endorsement correct?" Taishi Ci asked. "Let me see it.

sentences.zh: 取來視之。

translations.literal: Bring it and let me examine it.
translations.idiomatic: Hand it over for inspection.

sentences.zh: 」吏殊不知其東萊人也，因為取章。

translations.literal: The clerk in no way realized he was a man of Donglai and therefore fetched the memorial for him.
translations.idiomatic: Unaware that he faced a man from Donglai, the clerk produced the document.

sentences.zh: 慈已先懷刀，便截敗之。

translations.literal: Ci had already concealed a knife on his person; he then cut the memorial to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci had hidden a knife; he shredded the memorial on the spot.

sentences.zh: 吏踴躍大呼，言「人壞我章」！

translations.literal: The clerk leaped up and shouted, saying, "Someone has ruined my memorial!
translations.idiomatic: The clerk cried out, "He has destroyed my memorial!

sentences.zh: 慈將至車閒，與語曰：「向使君不以章相與，吾亦無因得敗之，是為吉凶禍福等耳，吾不獨受此罪。

translations.literal: Ci led him to the space between the carts and said to him, "If you, sir, had not given me the memorial, I likewise would have had no means to destroy it—thus blessing and misfortune are alike; I do not bear this guilt alone.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci drew him between the wagons: "Had you refused the document, I could not have torn it—good or ill, we share the blame equally.

sentences.zh: 豈若默然俱出去，可以存易亡，無事俱就刑辟。

translations.literal: Would it not be better silently to leave together? One may preserve life in place of death; otherwise we will both go to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Better we slip away together in silence—trade ruin for survival—than hang separately for nothing.

sentences.zh: 」吏言：「君為郡敗吾章，已得如意，欲復亡為？

translations.literal: The clerk said, "You ruined my memorial for the commandery and already got your wish—do you still wish to flee?
translations.idiomatic: "You shredded my memorial for their sake," the clerk shot back. "You have what you wanted—why run now?

sentences.zh: 」慈答曰：「初受郡遣，但來視章通與未耳。

translations.literal: Ci replied, "When I first received the commandery's commission, I came only to see whether the memorial had been submitted or not.
translations.idiomatic: "The commandery sent me," Taishi Ci answered, "only to learn whether your memorial had gone in.

sentences.zh: 吾用意太過，乃相敗章。

translations.literal: My intentions went too far, and so I destroyed the memorial together with you.
translations.idiomatic: I went further than intended and ruined it—with you.

sentences.zh: 今還，亦恐以此見譴怒，故俱欲去爾。

translations.literal: Now returning, I also fear being blamed and angered for this; therefore we both wish to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Going home I still face punishment over this—so flight suits us both.

sentences.zh: 」吏然慈言，即日俱去。

translations.literal: The clerk approved Ci's words; that same day they both departed.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk agreed; they fled together that very day.

sentences.zh: 慈既與出城，因遁還通郡章。

translations.literal: After Ci had gone out of the city with him, he slipped back and submitted the commandery's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Once outside the walls Taishi Ci doubled back and filed the commandery's petition.

sentences.zh: 州家聞之，更遣吏通章，有司以格章之故不復見理，州受其短。

translations.literal: When the provincial authorities heard of it, they sent another clerk to submit the memorial; the offices in charge, because of the irregularity with the memorial, no longer ruled on the case, and the province bore the fault.
translations.idiomatic: The province dispatched another clerk, but the boards refused the case—the mishandled paperwork left the provincial side at fault.

sentences.zh: 由是知名，而為州家所疾，恐受其禍，乃避之遼東。

translations.literal: By this he became renowned but was hated by the provincial authorities; fearing harm from them, he fled to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: The exploit made his name—and earned the provincial inspector's hatred—so he took refuge in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 北海相孔融聞而奇之，數遣人訊問其母，并致餉遺。

translations.literal: Chancellor of Beihai Kong Rong heard of him and considered him extraordinary, repeatedly sending men to inquire after his mother and also sending gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong, chancellor of Beihai, heard the tale and took notice, repeatedly inquiring after Taishi Ci's mother and sending presents.

sentences.zh: 時融以黃巾寇暴，出屯都昌，為賊管亥所圍。

translations.literal: At that time Rong, because of Yellow Turban raiding, went out and encamped at Duchang and was besieged by the bandit Guan Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Turban unrest had driven Kong Rong to camp at Duchang, where the outlaw Guan Hai surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 慈從遼東還，母謂慈曰：「汝與孔北海未嘗相見，至汝行後，贍恤殷勤，過於故舊，今為賊所圍，汝宜赴之。

translations.literal: When Ci returned from Liaodong, his mother said to him, "You and Kong of Beihai have never met; since you left, he has supported and comforted me more diligently than old friends—now he is besieged by bandits—you ought to go to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi Ci came home from Liaodong, his mother said, "You have never met Kong Rong, yet since you left he has cared for me more faithfully than old companions—now bandits hem him in—you must go.

sentences.zh: 」慈留三日，單步徑至都昌。

translations.literal: Ci stayed three days, then alone on foot went straight to Duchang.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci lingered three days, then walked alone straight to Duchang.

sentences.zh: 時圍尚未密，夜伺閒隙，得入見融，因求兵出斫賊。

translations.literal: At that time the siege was not yet tight; by night he watched for an opening, was able to enter and see Rong, and thereupon sought troops to go out and strike the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The ring was still loose; under cover of night he found a gap, slipped in to Kong Rong, and asked for sortie troops.

sentences.zh: 融不聽，欲待外救。

translations.literal: Rong would not listen and wished to await outside relief.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong refused, insisting on waiting for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 未有至者，而圍日偪。

translations.literal: None had arrived, while the siege closed tighter day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Relief never came and the noose tightened daily.

sentences.zh: 融欲告急平原相劉備，城中人無由得出，慈自請求行。

translations.literal: Rong wished to send urgent word to Chancellor of Pingyuan Liu Bei, but no one in the city could get out; Ci himself requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong needed to alert Liu Bei in Pingyuan, yet no one could break out—Taishi Ci volunteered.

sentences.zh: 融曰：「今賊圍甚密，眾人皆言不可，卿意雖壯，無乃實難乎？

translations.literal: Rong said, "Now the bandit siege is very tight; everyone says it cannot be done—though your intent is bold, is it not in truth difficult?
translations.idiomatic: "The rebels have sealed every gap," Kong Rong said. "All say it is impossible—your courage is great, but can you really do this?

sentences.zh: 」慈對曰：「昔府君傾意於老母，老母感遇，遣慈赴府君之急，固以慈有可取，而來必有益也。

translations.literal: Ci replied, "Formerly the lord lavished concern on my aged mother; my mother, moved by his kindness, sent me to answer the lord's emergency—she firmly believed I had something to offer and that my coming would bring benefit.
translations.idiomatic: "My mother sent me because you honored her," Taishi Ci replied. "She believed I could help you.

sentences.zh: 今眾人言不可，慈亦言不可，豈府君愛顧之義，老母遣慈之意邪？

translations.literal: Now everyone says it cannot be done, and Ci also says it cannot be done—is this the duty of care the lord showed, or the meaning of my mother's sending Ci?
translations.idiomatic: If everyone—including me—calls it hopeless, what becomes of your kindness and her charge?

sentences.zh: 事已急矣，願府君無疑。

translations.literal: The matter is already urgent; I beg the lord not to doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Time is short—please trust me.

sentences.zh: 」融乃然之。

translations.literal: Rong thereupon approved.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Rong consented.

sentences.zh: 於是嚴行蓐食，須明，便帶鞬攝弓上馬，將兩騎自隨，各作一的持之，開門直出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he strictly prepared travel rations; at dawn Ci belted his quiver, took up his bow, mounted his horse, and with two horsemen following, each holding a target, went straight out the gate.
translations.idiomatic: They packed a meal; at first light Taishi Ci slung his quiver, seized his bow, mounted with two riders—each man carrying a straw target—and rode straight through the gate.

sentences.zh: 外圍下左右人並驚駭，兵馬互出。

translations.literal: Those below the outer ring on left and right were all astonished; troops and horses rushed out on every side.
translations.idiomatic: Sentries along the berm recoiled as troops boiled forth.

sentences.zh: 慈引馬至城下塹內，植所持的各一，出射之，射之畢，徑入門。

translations.literal: Ci led his horse into the moat below the wall, planted the targets each held one apiece, rode out and shot them; when the shooting was finished, he went straight back inside the gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rode into the ditch, planted the targets, emptied his bow at them, and wheeled back inside.

sentences.zh: 明晨復如此，圍下人或起或臥，慈復植的，射之畢，復入門。

translations.literal: The next morning he did the same again; those below the siege line either rose or lay down; Ci again planted the targets, finished shooting, and again entered the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Next dawn he repeated the display—watchmen lounged or slept—then planted fresh targets, shot them clear, and slipped back in.

sentences.zh: 明晨復出如此，無復起者，於是下鞭馬直突圍中馳去。

translations.literal: The next morning he went out thus again; no one rose anymore; thereupon he whipped his horse and charged straight through the siege line and galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: On the third morning no one stirred to stop him; he spurred through the lines and vanished.

sentences.zh: 比賊覺知，慈行已過，又射殺數人，皆應弦而倒，故無敢追者。

translations.literal: By the time the bandits realized, Ci had already passed; he also shot down several men who all fell at the bowstring's twang—therefore none dared pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Before the rebels reacted he was gone, dropping pursuers with each shot until none followed.

sentences.zh: 遂到平原，說備曰：「慈，東萊之鄙人也，與孔北海親非骨肉，比非鄉黨，特以名志相好，有分災共患之義。

translations.literal: He reached Pingyuan and said to Bei, "Ci is a humble man of Donglai—I am not bone kin to Kong of Beihai nor fellow townsman—I merely cherish him by reputation and intent and hold to sharing disaster and peril.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingyuan he told Liu Bei, "I am a nobody from Donglai—not Kong Rong's kin nor neighbor—yet name and honor bind us to share peril.

sentences.zh: 今管亥暴亂，北海被圍，孤窮無援，危在旦夕。

translations.literal: Now Guan Hai runs riot; Beihai is besieged; isolated and without aid, danger hangs by dawn and dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Hai ravages the land; Beihai is ringed and alone—ruin is hours away.

sentences.zh: 以君有仁義之名，能救人之急，故北海區區，延頸恃仰，使慈冒白刃，突重圍，從萬死之中自託於君，惟君所以存之。

translations.literal: Because you, sir, bear a reputation for benevolence and righteousness and can rescue men in extremity, therefore poor Beihai stretches its neck and waits in hope; he sent Ci to brave naked blades and burst the tight siege, from amid ten thousand deaths entrusting himself to you—howsoever you preserve them.
translations.idiomatic: They say you are humane—you save the desperate—so Beihai cranes its neck toward you. I broke through at sword's edge to beg your aid.

sentences.zh: 」備斂容答曰：「孔北海知世間有劉備邪！

translations.literal: Bei composed himself and replied, "Does Kong of Beihai know there is a Liu Bei in the world!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei straightened: "Kong Rong knows there is a Liu Bei in this world!

sentences.zh: 」即遣精兵三千人隨慈。

translations.literal: Immediately he dispatched three thousand picked troops to follow Ci.
translations.idiomatic: He detached three thousand veterans at once.

sentences.zh: 賊聞兵至，解圍散走。

translations.literal: When the bandits heard troops had arrived, they lifted the siege and scattered in flight.
translations.idiomatic: At word of soldiers the besiegers melted away.

sentences.zh: 融既得濟，益奇貴慈，曰：「卿吾之少友也。

translations.literal: Once Rong had escaped danger, he esteemed Ci all the more as extraordinary and said, "You are my young friend.
translations.idiomatic: Delivered, Kong Rong prized Taishi Ci still higher: "You are the friend of my youth.

sentences.zh: 」事畢，還啟其母，母曰：「我喜汝有以報孔北海也。」

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, he returned and reported to his mother; his mother said, "I am pleased that you had means to repay Kong of Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci reported home; his mother said, "I rejoice that you could repay Kong Rong.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史劉繇與慈同郡，慈自遼東還，未與相見，暫渡江到曲阿見繇，未去，會孫策至。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yang Province Liu Yao was from the same commandery as Ci; when Ci returned from Liaodong he had not yet met him—he crossed the river for a time to Qu'e to see Yao and had not yet left when Sun Ce arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, inspector of Yang Province, shared Taishi Ci's homeland. Returning from Liaodong, Taishi Ci crossed to Qu'e to join him—Sun Ce arrived before he could depart.

sentences.zh: 或勸繇可以慈為大將軍，繇曰：「我若用子義，許子將不當笑我邪？

translations.literal: Someone urged Yao that he could employ Ci as Grand General; Yao said, "If I employ Ziyi, will not Xu Zijiang laugh at me?
translations.idiomatic: Counselors said appoint Taishi Ci commander—Liu Yao answered, "Would Xu Shao not mock me?

sentences.zh: 」但使慈偵視輕重。

translations.literal: He only had Ci reconnoiter and weigh the enemy situation.
translations.idiomatic: He used Taishi Ci only as a scout.

sentences.zh: 時獨與一騎卒遇策。

translations.literal: At that time he alone with one mounted soldier encountered Ce.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci met Sun Ce with a single trooper.

sentences.zh: 策從騎十三，皆韓當、宋謙、黃蓋輩也。

translations.literal: Ce had thirteen riders with him, all men like Han Dang, Song Qian, and Huang Gai.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce brought thirteen horsemen—Han Dang, Song Qian, Huang Gai, and their ilk.

sentences.zh: 慈便前鬥，正與策對。

translations.literal: Ci went forward to fight and faced Ce directly.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci rode out and traded blows with Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策刺慈馬，而攬得慈項上手戟，慈亦得策兜鍪。

translations.literal: Ce stabbed Ci's horse and seized the halberd Ci held at his neck; Ci likewise seized Ce's helmet.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce lanced Taishi Ci's mount and snatched the halberd at his collar; Taishi Ci tore off Sun Ce's helmet.

sentences.zh: 會兩家兵騎並各來赴，於是解散。

translations.literal: Just then both sides' troops and cavalry came rushing up together; thereupon they broke off.
translations.idiomatic: Then both armies poured in and they separated.

sentences.zh: 慈當與繇俱奔豫章，而遁於蕪湖，亡入山中，稱丹楊太守。

translations.literal: Ci was to flee with Yao to Yuzhang but slipped away to Wuhu, fled into the mountains, and styled himself Grand Administrator of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: He should have withdrawn to Yuzhang with Liu Yao but broke for Wuhu, hid in the hills, and proclaimed himself grand administrator of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 是時，策已平定宣城以東，惟涇以西六縣未服。

translations.literal: By then Ce had already pacified everything east of Xuancheng; only the six counties west of Jing had not submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had already cleared the country east of Xuancheng; six counties west of the Jing River still held out.

sentences.zh: 慈因進住涇縣，立屯府，大為山越所附。

translations.literal: Ci therefore advanced and stationed himself in Jing county, set up a camp headquarters, and was greatly joined by the mountain Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci advanced into Jing county, threw up a base, and drew heavy support from the mountain Yue.

sentences.zh: 策躬自攻討，遂見囚執。

translations.literal: Ce personally campaigned against him and thereupon took him prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce attacked in person and captured him.

sentences.zh: 策即解縛，捉其手曰：「寧識神亭時邪？

translations.literal: Ce immediately undid his bonds, grasped his hand, and said, "Do you recall Shenting?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce freed him at once, seized his hand, and asked, "Remember Shenting?

sentences.zh: 若卿爾時得我云何？

translations.literal: If you had gotten me then, what would you have done?
translations.idiomatic: If you had caught me then, what then?

sentences.zh: 」慈曰：「未可量也。

translations.literal: Ci said, "It could not be measured.
translations.idiomatic: "Hard to say," Taishi Ci replied.

sentences.zh: 」策大笑曰：「今日之事，當與卿共之。」

translations.literal: Ce laughed greatly and said, "Today's affair—I shall share it with you.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce roared with laughter: "From today we share one fortune.

sentences.zh: 〈《吴历》云：慈於神亭战败，为策所执。

translations.literal: The Wu Calendar states: Ci was defeated at Shenting and captured by Ce.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Calendar records that Taishi Ci was defeated at Shenting and captured by Sun Ce.

sentences.zh: 策素闻其名，即解缚请见，咨问进取之术。

translations.literal: Ce had long heard his fame, immediately released his bonds and invited audience, and consulted him on methods of advance.
translations.idiomatic: —yet Sun Ce had admired him for years, cut his bonds, received him, and asked strategy.

sentences.zh: 慈答曰：“破军之将，不足与论事。

translations.literal: Ci replied, "A general of a broken army is not worth discussing affairs with.
translations.idiomatic: "A beaten commander is poor company for counsel.

sentences.zh: ”策曰：“昔韩信定计於广武，今策决疑於仁者，君何辞焉？

translations.literal: Ce said, "Formerly Han Xin laid plans at Guangwu; now Ce resolves doubts with a man of benevolence—why do you decline?
translations.idiomatic: "Han Xin planned at Guangwu," Sun Ce said. "I settle doubt with a gentleman—why refuse?

sentences.zh: ”慈曰：“州军新破，士卒离心，若傥分散，难复合聚；

translations.literal: Ci said, "The provincial army is newly broken and the soldiers' hearts are divided—if by chance they scatter, it will be hard to gather them again;
translations.idiomatic: "Your provincial troops are shattered and demoralized—scatter them and you will never reassemble them.

sentences.zh: 欲出宣恩安集，恐不合尊意。

translations.literal: I wish to go forth and spread favor to pacify and gather them, but fear this may not accord with your honored intent.
translations.idiomatic: I propose to tour them with generous words—but only if that suits you.

sentences.zh: ”策长跪答曰：“诚本心所望也。

translations.literal: Ce knelt long and replied, "That is truly what my heart hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce knelt: "It is exactly what I wish.

sentences.zh: 明日中，望君来还。

translations.literal: By noon tomorrow I look for you to return.
translations.idiomatic: Return to me by noon tomorrow.

sentences.zh: ”诸将皆疑，策曰：“太史子义，青州名士，以信义为先，终不欺策。

translations.literal: The generals all doubted; Ce said, "Taishi Ziyi is a famous scholar of Qingzhou—he puts good faith first and will never deceive Ce.
translations.idiomatic: His officers murmured doubt; Sun Ce said, "Taishi Ci is a Qingzhou gentleman of honor—he will not betray me.

sentences.zh: ”明日，大请诸将，豫设酒食，立竿视影。

translations.literal: The next day he greatly feasted the generals, beforehand setting out wine and food, planted a pole and watched its shadow.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he feasted his commanders, set wine in advance, and marked noon with a pole's shadow.

sentences.zh: 日中而慈至，策大悦，常与参论诸军事。

translations.literal: At midday Ci arrived; Ce was greatly pleased and constantly consulted with him on various military matters.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci appeared at noon; Sun Ce rejoiced and kept him at council.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案；

translations.literal: Your subject Pei Songzhi remarks:
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes:

sentences.zh: 吴历云慈於神亭战败，为策所得，与本传大异，疑为谬误。

translations.literal: The Wu Calendar says Ci was defeated at Shenting and obtained by Ce; this greatly differs from this biography—I suspect it is mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Calendar's tale of defeat and capture contradicts the main text and is probably wrong.

sentences.zh: 《江表传》曰：策问慈曰：“闻卿昔为太守劫州章，赴文举，请诣玄德，皆有烈义，天下智士也，但所讬未得其人。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce asked Ci, "I have heard that formerly you seized the provincial memorial for the grand administrator, rushed to Wenju, and went to pay call on Xuande—all deeds of fierce righteousness; you are a wise man of the All-under-Heaven—but those you relied on were not the right men.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan quotes Sun Ce: "They say you seized the inspector's memorial for your lord, raced to Kong Rong, and sought Liu Bei—heroic acts—yet you backed the wrong patrons.

sentences.zh: 射钩斩袪，古人不嫌。

translations.literal: Shooting the hook and cutting the sleeve—the ancients did not shrink from such.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies overlooked far worse slights.

sentences.zh: 孤是卿知己，勿忧不如意也。

translations.literal: I am your knowing friend—do not worry that things will not go as you wish.
translations.idiomatic: I am your true ally—do not fear disappointment.

sentences.zh: ”出教曰：“龙欲腾翥，先阶尺木者也。”〉

translations.literal: He issued a directive saying, "The dragon that would soar first mounts a foot of wood."
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "Before the dragon can leap skyward it needs a perch—even a span of timber."

sentences.zh: 即署門下督，還吳授兵，拜折衝中郎將。

translations.literal: Immediately he appointed him corps commander of the headquarters guard, returned to Wu to hand him troops, and appointed him General of the Household Who Crushes the Foe.
translations.idiomatic: He named Taishi Ci headquarters gate captain, sent him to Wu for a command, and commissioned him General of the Household Who Crushes the Foe.

sentences.zh: 後劉繇亡於豫章，士眾萬餘人未有所附，策命慈往撫安焉。

translations.literal: Later Liu Yao died in Yuzhang; more than ten thousand soldiers and followers had none to attach to; Ce ordered Ci to go comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yao died at Yuzhang, ten thousand men stood leaderless—Sun Ce sent Taishi Ci to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策谓慈曰：“刘牧往责吾为袁氏攻庐江，其意颇猥，理恕不足。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: Ce said to Ci, "Formerly Governor Liu came to blame me for attacking Lujiang on Yuan Shao's behalf—his meaning was rather base, and forgiveness was hardly adequate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan records Sun Ce telling Taishi Ci: "Liu Yao once reproached me for storming Lujiang at Yuan Shu's bidding—petty logic, hardly worth pardon.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 先君手下兵数千餘人，尽在公路许。

translations.literal: My late lord's troops under his command, several thousand odd men, were all in Yuan Shu's keeping.
translations.idiomatic: The several thousand veterans my father once commanded were entirely in Yuan Shu's hands.

sentences.zh: 孤志在立事，不得不屈意於公路，求索故兵，再往才得千餘人耳。

translations.literal: I aim to accomplish something and had to humble my mind toward Gonglu—begging back those former troops—only after going twice did I obtain a little over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: I meant to build a power base, so I swallowed my pride with Yuan Shu and pleaded for my father's old soldiers—two trips won me barely a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 仍令孤攻庐江，尔时事势，不得不为行。

translations.literal: He still ordered me to attack Lujiang; given the situation of that time, I had no choice but to go.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered me against Lujiang anyway; in those circumstances I could hardly refuse.

sentences.zh: 但其后不遵臣节，自弃作邪僭事，谏之不从。

translations.literal: But afterward he did not observe a minister's duty and threw himself into wicked usurpation; when remonstrated he would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Then he cast aside every obligation as a subject and turned to treason; counsel left him unmoved.

sentences.zh: 丈夫义交，苟有大故，不得不离，孤交求公路及绝之本末如此。

translations.literal: When men of honor bond in righteousness, if a grave cause arises they must part—the beginning and end of my dealings with Gonglu and how I broke with him were thus.
translations.idiomatic: Honorable men may ally in good faith, but grave offense forces a breach—that is the whole tale of how I served Yuan Shu and how I left him.

sentences.zh: 今刘繇丧亡，恨不及其生时与共论辩。

translations.literal: Now Liu Yao is dead—I regret that I could not debate these matters with him while he lived.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao is gone; I mourn that we never argued out these points face to face.

sentences.zh: 今兒子在豫章，不知华子鱼待遇何如，其故复曲复依随之否？

translations.literal: His son is now in Yuzhang—I do not know how Hua Ziyu treats him, or whether his former followers still twist themselves to follow along.
translations.idiomatic: The boy remains in Yuzhang—I cannot tell how Hua Xin receives him, or whether Liu Yao's old retainers still cling to him.

sentences.zh: 卿则州人，昔又从事，宁能往视其兒子，并宣孤意於其部曲？

translations.literal: You are a fellow native of the province and once served him—could you go observe his son and proclaim my intentions to his personal troops?
translations.idiomatic: You hail from the same province and once served under Liu Yao—will you visit his son and explain my purpose to his officers and men?

sentences.zh: 部曲乐来者便与俱来，不乐来者且安慰之。

translations.literal: Among his troops, those glad to come may come with you; those not glad to come, for now comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Welcome anyone willing to follow you; reassure those who prefer to stay.

sentences.zh: 并观察子鱼所以牧御方规何似，视庐陵、鄱阳人民亲附之否？

translations.literal: Also observe by what methods Hua Ziyu herds and governs, and see whether the people of Luling and Poyang attach themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Watch how Hua Xin rules—whether Luling and Poyang truly accept his authority.

sentences.zh: 卿手下兵，宜将多少，自由意。

translations.literal: As for how many troops you should lead—follow your own intent.
translations.idiomatic: Take whatever force you judge sufficient—the choice is yours.

sentences.zh: ”慈对曰：“慈有不赦之罪，将军量同桓、文，待遇过望。

translations.literal: Ci replied, "Ci bears crimes deserving no pardon; the General measures himself like Duke Huan and Lord Wen—your kindness surpasses what I dared hope.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci answered, "I am guilty beyond forgiveness; you rank yourself with the great hegemons of old—your favor overwhelms me.

sentences.zh: 古人报生以死，期於尽节，没而后已。

translations.literal: The ancients repaid one who gave them life with death, aiming to exhaust their fidelity—they ceased only when life ended.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients gave their lives to repay a patron, holding nothing back until death.

sentences.zh: 今并息兵，兵不宜多，将数十人，自足以往还也。”〉

translations.literal: Now arms are stilled everywhere—troops ought not be numerous; leading several tens of men is enough for the journey there and back.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is quiet—I need no large escort; a few dozen riders will suffice for the round trip.

sentences.zh: 左右皆曰：「慈必北去不還。

translations.literal: Those around him all said, "Ci will surely go north and not return.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers warned, "Taishi Ci will flee north and never come back.

sentences.zh: 」策曰：「子義捨我，當復與誰？

translations.literal: Ce said, "If Ziyi leaves me, whom else should he join?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce replied, "If Ziyi abandons me, whom would he serve instead?

sentences.zh: 」餞送昌門，把腕別曰：「何時能還？

translations.literal: They escorted him with a farewell feast at Chang Gate, grasping wrists in parting: "When can you return?
translations.idiomatic: At Chang Gate they drank his farewell and clasped wrists: "When will we see you again?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「不過六十日。

translations.literal: He answered, "No more than sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: "Inside sixty days."

sentences.zh: 」果如期而反。

translations.literal: He indeed returned at the appointed time.
translations.idiomatic: He returned exactly on schedule.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：策初遣慈，议者纷纭，谓慈未可信，或云与华子鱼州里，恐留彼为筹策，或疑慈西讬黄祖，假路还北，多言遣之非计。

translations.literal: The Jiangbiao zhuan states: When Ce first dispatched Ci, debaters wrangled—some said Ci could not be trusted; some said he was fellow townsman with Hua Ziyu and feared he would stay there plotting; some suspected Ci would entrust himself west to Huang Zu and borrow a road back north—many said sending him was no plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangbiao zhuan notes that when Sun Ce first sent Taishi Ci away, critics quarreled: some doubted his loyalty; some feared he would collude with fellow townsman Hua Xin; others suspected he would detour through Huang Zu and bolt north—most called the mission folly.

sentences.zh: 策曰：“诸君语皆非也，孤断之详矣。

translations.literal: Ce said, "Sirs, your words are all wrong—I have judged this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce said, "You are mistaken—I have thought this through.

sentences.zh: 太史子义虽气勇有胆烈，然非纵横之人。

translations.literal: Taishi Ziyi, though fierce of spirit and brave of daring, is not a conniving horizontal strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci is bold and daring, not the sort to intrigue among factions.

sentences.zh: 其心有士谟，志经道义，贵重然诺，一以意许知己，死亡不相负，诸君勿复忧也。

translations.literal: His heart holds the planning of a knight; his ambition threads the Way and duty; he esteems his promises—once he agrees in spirit with a friend who knows him, he will not betray him even in death—sirs, fret no more.
translations.idiomatic: His mind is that of a gentleman-officer; he follows duty and keeps faith—once he pledges himself to a kindred soul, he dies before he breaks his word. Cease your worrying.

sentences.zh: ”慈从豫章还，议者乃始服。

translations.literal: When Ci returned from Yuzhang, the debaters at last submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Taishi Ci came back from Yuzhang, his critics fell silent.

sentences.zh: 慈见策曰：“华子鱼良德也，然非筹略才，无他方规，自守而已。

translations.literal: Ci saw Ce and said, "Hua Ziyu is a man of fine virtue, yet he is no strategist—he has no larger design; he merely holds his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci reported: "Hua Xin is decent enough but no planner—he has no grand scheme beyond digging in.

sentences.zh: 又丹杨僮芝自擅庐陵，诈言被诏书为太守。

translations.literal: Moreover Tong Zhi of Danyang has arrogated Luling to himself, falsely claiming an imperial edict appointed him grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Tong Zhi of Danyang has seized Luling on forged orders.

sentences.zh: 鄱阳民帅别立宗部，阻兵守界，不受子鱼所遣长吏，言‘我以别立郡，须汉遣真太守来，当迎之耳’。

translations.literal: The militia leaders of Poyang have separately erected lineage levies, blocking arms and guarding borders; they do not accept the senior officials Ziyu dispatches, saying, "We have set up a separate commandery—we must wait until Han sends a true grand administrator; then we will welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang chiefs have raised private militias along the frontier and refuse Hua Xin's appointees: "We have proclaimed our own district—we want an imperial grand administrator before we yield.

sentences.zh: 子鱼不但不能谐庐陵、鄱阳，近自海昬有上缭壁，有五六千家相结聚作宗伍，惟输租布於郡耳，发召一人遂不可得，子鱼亦睹视之而已。

translations.literal: Ziyu cannot even harmonize Luling and Poyang; recently from Haihun there is the Shangliao rampart—five or six thousand households have banded together as a lineage corps; they only deliver rent cloth to the commandery—summon a single man and you cannot obtain him—Ziyu merely watches and does nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Xin cannot pacify Luling or Poyang. Near Haihun the Shangliao stockade holds five or six thousand households in clan bands—they pay only cloth tribute and ignore every levy; Hua Xin simply looks on.

sentences.zh: ”策拊掌大笑，

translations.literal: Ce clapped his hands and laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce slapped his thigh and roared with laughter.

translations.literal: (still)
translations.idiomatic: (emphatic: he)

sentences.zh: 有兼并之志矣。

translations.literal: already harbored ambition to annex.
translations.idiomatic: already nursed designs on annexing the region.

sentences.zh: 顷之，遂定豫章。〉

translations.literal: Before long, Yuzhang was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Yuzhang lay firmly in hand.

sentences.zh: 劉表從子磐，驍勇，數為寇於艾、西安諸縣。

translations.literal: Liu Pan, Liu Biao's elder brother's son, was fierce and brave and repeatedly raided as a bandit in the counties of Ai and Xi'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Biao's nephew Liu Pan was a fierce fighter who repeatedly harried the Ai and Xi'an districts.

sentences.zh: 策於是分海昏、建昌左右六縣，以慈為建昌都尉，治海昏，并督諸將拒磐。

translations.literal: Ce therefore divided the six counties around Haihun and Jianchang, appointed Ci as commandant of Jianchang with headquarters at Haihun, and had him oversee the various generals resisting Pan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce carved out six counties around Haihun and Jianchang, named Taishi Ci commandant of Jianchang based at Haihun, and told him to coordinate defense against Liu Pan.

sentences.zh: 磐絕跡不復為寇。

translations.literal: Pan vanished from sight and no longer raided.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Pan withdrew and struck no more raids.

sentences.zh: 慈長七尺七寸，美鬚髯，猿臂善射，弦不虛發。

translations.literal: Ci stood seven chi seven cun tall, handsome of beard, ape-armed and skilled at archery—the bowstring never sounded without a hit.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci stood seven feet seven inches, with a splendid beard and long arms—an archer whose every arrow flew true.

sentences.zh: 嘗從策討麻保賊，賊於屯裏緣樓上行詈，以手持樓棼，慈引弓射之，矢貫手著棼，圍外萬人莫不稱善。

translations.literal: Once when accompanying Ce against the Ma Bao bandits, the bandits on the rampart walk atop their stockade reviled them, hands gripping the gallery beams; Ci drew his bow and shot—the arrow pierced the hand and pinned it to the beam—outside the siege ten thousand men cried excellent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Ma Bao campaign the rebels stood on their parapet cursing, hands on the rafters; Taishi Ci drove an arrow through palm and timber alike—the army below roared approval.

sentences.zh: 其妙如此。

translations.literal: His skill was thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his marksmanship.

sentences.zh: 曹公聞其名，遺慈書，以篋封之，發省無所道，而但貯當歸。

translations.literal: Duke Cao heard his fame and sent Ci a letter sealed in a document case; opening and examining it, there was nothing written—only angelica root stored inside.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao sent a sealed packet bearing only angelica—a pun urging him to "return" (danggui homophone).

sentences.zh: 孫權統事，以慈能制磐，遂委南方之事。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan took charge of affairs, because Ci could restrain Pan, he entrusted southern matters to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan, knowing Taishi Ci could hold Liu Pan in check, gave him the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 年四十一，建安十一年卒。

translations.literal: At forty-one years he died in the eleventh year of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-one in Jian'an 206.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：慈临亡，叹息曰：“丈夫生世，当带七尺之剑，以升天子之阶。

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: As Ci faced death he sighed and said, "A man born into this world ought to gird a seven-chi sword and ascend the steps to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book records his dying sigh: "A man should belt a seven-foot blade and climb the palace stairs.

sentences.zh: 今所志未从，奈何而死乎！

translations.literal: What I aspired to has not been granted—how can I die!
translations.idiomatic: My ambitions lie unfulfilled—must I die now?

sentences.zh: ”权甚悼惜之。〉

translations.literal: Quan deeply mourned and pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan grieved deeply for him.

sentences.zh: 子享，官至越騎校尉。

translations.literal: His son Xiang rose to Colonel of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His son Taishi Xiang rose to Colonel of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：享字元复，历尚书、吴郡太守。〉

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: Xiang's courtesy name was Yuanfu; he served as Palace Secretariat Director and Grand Administrator of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book gives Xiang the style Yuanfu and lists posts at the secretariat and as grand administrator of Wu.

sentences.zh: 士燮字威彥，蒼梧廣信人也。

translations.literal: Shi Xie, courtesy name Weiyan, was a native of Guangxin in Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie, styled Weiyan, came from Guangxin in Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 其先本魯國汶陽人，至王莽之亂，避地交州。

translations.literal: His ancestors were originally from Wenyang in the state of Lu; at the turmoil of Wang Mang they fled and settled in Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The family hailed from Wenyang in Lu but relocated to Jiaozhou during Wang Mang's upheaval.

sentences.zh: 六世至燮父賜，桓帝時為日南太守。

translations.literal: Six generations down to Xie's father Ci—under Emperor Huan he was Grand Administrator of Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: Six generations later came Xie's father Shi Ci, grand administrator of Rinan under Emperor Huan.

sentences.zh: 燮少游學京師，事潁川劉子奇，治左氏春秋。

translations.literal: Xie in youth traveled to study in the capital and studied under Liu Ziqi of Yingchuan, mastering the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Shi Xie studied in Luoyang under Liu Ziqi of Yingchuan, specializing in the Zuo commentary.

sentences.zh: 察孝廉，補尚書郎，公事免官。

translations.literal: Recommended as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed Gentleman of the Palace and dismissed from office over official business.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filial and incorrupt, he entered the palace corps but lost his post over an administrative matter.

sentences.zh: 父賜喪闋後，舉茂才，除巫令，遷交阯太守。

translations.literal: After his father Ci's mourning was completed, he was nominated as Outstanding Talent, appointed magistrate of Wu, and promoted to Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning for his father ended he earned nomination as Outstanding Talent, served as magistrate of Wu district, then rose to grand administrator of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 弟壹，初為郡督郵。

translations.literal: Younger brother Yi—at first was commandery Recording Officer.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shi Yi began as the commandery Recording Officer.

sentences.zh: 刺史丁宮徵還京都，壹侍送勤恪，宮感之，臨別謂曰：「刺史若待罪三事，當相辟也。

translations.literal: Inspector Ding Gong was summoned back to the capital; Yi attended him in escort with diligent care; Gong was moved and on parting said to him, "If this inspector bears guilt among the Three Ducal Offices, I shall summon you.
translations.idiomatic: When Inspector Ding Gong returned to the capital, Shi Yi escorted him faithfully; Ding Gong promised, "Should I rise to one of the Three Excellencies, I will call for you.

sentences.zh: 」後宮為司徒，辟壹。

translations.literal: Later Gong became Minister of Education and summoned Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Gong later became Minister of Education and summoned Shi Yi.

sentences.zh: 比至，宮已免，黃琬代為司徒，甚禮遇壹。

translations.literal: By the time Yi arrived Gong had already been dismissed; Huang Wan replaced him as Minister of Education and treated Yi with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi arrived too late—Ding Gong had fallen; Huang Wan, the new minister of education, honored him nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 董卓作亂，壹亡歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Dong Zhuo launched rebellion; Yi fled back to his homeland.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo seized power Shi Yi fled home.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：琬与卓相害，而壹尽心於琬，甚有声称。

translations.literal: The Wu Book states: Though Wan and Zhuo harmed each other, Yi devoted his utmost to Wan and enjoyed high reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu Book notes that despite Huang Wan's feud with Dong Zhuo, Shi Yi served Huang Wan loyally and earned wide praise.

sentences.zh: 卓恶之，乃署教曰：“司徒掾士壹，不得除用。

translations.literal: Zhuo detested this and therefore issued an instruction saying, "Clerk Shi Yi of the Minister of Education may not be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhuo struck back with an order: "Do not assign any post to Minister of Education clerk Shi Yi.

sentences.zh: ”故历年不迁。

translations.literal: Therefore for successive years he was not promoted.
translations.idiomatic: For years Shi Yi could win no promotion.

sentences.zh: 会卓入关，壹乃亡归。〉

translations.literal: When Zhuo entered the Pass, Yi then fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhuo marched west Shi Yi escaped homeward again.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史朱符為夷賊所殺，州郡擾亂。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhou Zhu Fu was killed by barbarian bandits; the province and commanderies were in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian raiders slew Inspector Zhu Fu; the province collapsed into chaos.

sentences.zh: 燮乃表壹領合浦太守，次弟徐聞令䵋領九真太守，

translations.literal: Xie thereupon memorialized for Yi to serve as Grand Administrator of Hepu and for his next younger brother Wei, Magistrate of Xuwen
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie memorialized to appoint Shi Yi grand administrator of Hepu and his younger brother Wei—magistrate of Xuwen—

sentences.zh: 〈䵋音于鄙反，见《字林》。〉

translations.literal: 〈The graph used for Wei's personal name is read yu-bi fan; see the Zilin lexicon.〉
translations.idiomatic: Phonetic gloss for the rare graph in Wei's given name: read yu-bi fan per the Zilin dictionary.

sentences.zh: 䵋弟武，領南海太守。

translations.literal: to serve as Grand Administrator of Jiuzhen; Wei's younger brother Wu—appointed Grand Administrator of Nanhai.
translations.idiomatic: —as grand administrator of Jiuzhen, while Wei's youngest brother Shi Wu took Nanhai.

sentences.zh: 燮體器寬厚，謙虛下士，中國士人往依避難者以百數。

translations.literal: Xie was broad of bearing and tolerant, humble toward gentlemen—scholars from the Central Plains who went to rely on him and escape calamity numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie was magnanimous and modest before scholars; hundreds of refugees from the north sought shelter with him.

sentences.zh: 耽玩春秋，為之注解。

translations.literal: He immersed himself in the Spring and Autumn Annals and composed commentary on them.
translations.idiomatic: He steeped himself in the Spring and Autumn Annals and wrote his own commentary.

sentences.zh: 陳國袁徽與尚書令荀彧書曰：「交阯士府君既學問優博，又達於從政，處大亂之中，保全一郡，二十餘年疆埸無事，民不失業，羇旅之徒，皆蒙其慶，雖竇融保河西，曷以加之？

translations.literal: Yuan Hui of Chen state wrote to Minister Director Xun Yu saying, "Lord Shi of Jiaozhi is both broadly learned and adept at governance; amid great turmoil he has preserved a whole commandery for more than twenty years with quiet borders—his people keep their livelihoods, and wandering travelers all receive his blessings—even Dou Rong guarding Hexi—how could one add more?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hui wrote Xun Yu praising Shi Xie: learned and politically skilled, he kept Jiaozhi peaceful for twenty years while the empire burned—his folk stayed productive and refugees flourished—surpassing even Dou Rong's Hexi bulwark.

sentences.zh: 官事小闋，輒玩習書傳，春秋左氏傳尤簡練精微，吾數以咨問傳中諸疑，皆有師說，意思甚密。

translations.literal: When official duties allowed slight respite he always reviewed texts and transmissions; the Zuo Tradition he handled with especial terse refinement—I repeatedly consulted him on doubtful passages in the commentary—each had master's explanations—the meaning was very tight.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever duties eased he returned to his books; his grasp of the Zuo Tradition was razor-sharp—every knot I raised carried a teacher's gloss.

sentences.zh: 又尚書兼通古今，大義詳備。

translations.literal: Moreover he has mastered the Documents through ancient and modern—the great principles are detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the Documents ancient and modern alike—its core doctrines fully mapped.

sentences.zh: 聞京師古今之學，是非忿爭，今欲條左氏、尚書長義上之。

translations.literal: I hear that in the capital the learning of ancient versus modern Documents brawls over right and wrong—now I wish to lay out the extended meanings of the Zuo Tradition and Documents for submission upward.
translations.idiomatic: While Luoyang quarrels over Old versus New Text Documents, he plans to submit extended glosses on both the Zuo commentary and the Documents.

sentences.zh: 」其見稱如此。

translations.literal: Thus he was praised.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem he commanded.

sentences.zh: 燮兄弟並為列郡，雄長一州，偏在萬里，威尊無上。

translations.literal: The Xie brothers simultaneously held neighboring commanderies, dominating a whole province, tilted ten thousand li away—with awe-inspiring supremacy none could match.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi brothers ruled neighboring commanderies like kings of the far south—remote, unrivaled, supreme.

sentences.zh: 出入鳴鍾磬，備具威儀，笳簫鼓吹，車騎滿道，胡人夾轂焚燒香者常有數十。

translations.literal: Going out and coming in they sounded bells and sonorous stones, fully equipped with majestic ritual display—reed pipes, panpipes, drums, and bugles—carriages and riders filling the roads—often several tens of Hu pressing incense burners beside the wheel hubs.
