translations.idiomatic: Their processions rang bells and stones, paraded full ritual bands, and clogged the roads—foreign followers swinging censers from the carriage rails.

sentences.zh: 妻妾乘輜軿，子弟從兵騎，當時貴重，震服百蠻，尉他不足踰也。

translations.literal: Concubines rode in curtained wagons; sons and nephews followed with armored cavalry—esteemed as the highest nobility of the age—they awed the hundred barbarians—Zhao Tuo could not surpass them.
translations.idiomatic: Their women rode in silk coaches; sons and nephews rode escort—mightier than any southern lord since Zhao Tuo.

sentences.zh: 〈葛洪《神仙传》曰：燮尝病死，已三日，仙人董奉以一丸药与服，以水含之，捧其头摇

translations.literal: Ge Hong's Traditions of Divine Transcendents states: Xie once fell ill and died; already three days had passed when the transcendent Dong Feng gave him one pellet of medicine to take, washed down with water held in the mouth, grasped his head and shook
translations.idiomatic: Ge Hong recounts that Shi Xie apparently died for three days until the immortal Dong Feng fed him a pill, rinsed his mouth with water, seized his head and shook

translations.literal: (shake)
translations.idiomatic: (variant graph for "shake")

sentences.zh: 之，食顷，即开目动手，颜色渐复，半日能起坐，四日复能语，遂复常。

translations.literal: it; after about a mealtime he opened his eyes and moved his hands; his color gradually recovered; in half a day he could rise and sit; after four days he could speak again—thereupon he returned to normal.
translations.idiomatic: it—within minutes his eyes flickered and his fingers stirred; color returned to his cheeks; by midday he sat up; on the fourth day he spoke normally again.

sentences.zh: 奉字君异，侯官人也。〉

translations.literal: Feng's courtesy name was Junyi; he was a native of Houguan.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Feng, styled Junyi, hailed from Houguan.

sentences.zh: 武先病沒。

translations.literal: Wu died first of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Wu died first of sickness.

sentences.zh: 朱符死後，漢遣張津為交州刺史，津後又為其將區景所殺，而荊州牧劉表遣零陵賴恭代津。

translations.literal: After Zhu Fu's death Han dispatched Zhang Jin as Inspector of Jiaozhou; Jin afterward was also killed by his general Ou Jing, while Governor of Jing Province Liu Biao sent Lai Gong of Lingling to replace Jin.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Fu's murder the court named Zhang Jin inspector of Jiaozhou; Ou Jing killed him, so Liu Biao installed Lai Gong of Lingling in his stead.

sentences.zh: 是時蒼梧太守史璜死，表又遣吳巨代之，與恭俱至。

translations.literal: At that time Grand Administrator of Cangwu Shi Huang died; Biao also sent Wu Ju to replace him—Ju arrived together with Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Cangwu's grand administrator Shi Huang died, Liu Biao sent Wu Ju—who arrived alongside Lai Gong.

sentences.zh: 漢聞張津死，賜燮璽書曰：「交州絕域，南帶江海，上恩不宣，下義壅隔，知逆賊劉表又遣賴恭闚看南土，今以燮為綏南中郎將，董督七郡，領交阯太守如故。

translations.literal: Han heard Zhang Jin had died and granted Xie an imperial rescript saying, "Jiaozhou is a distant frontier, southern rim touching river and sea—superior grace does not reach downward and inferior duty is blocked—I know the rebel Liu Biao again sent Lai Gong to spy on the southern lands—now I appoint Xie General Who Pacifies the South, superintendent of seven commanderies, continuing concurrently as Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of Zhang Jin's death, the court messaged Shi Xie: the far south needed his stewardship; Liu Biao's spy Lai Gong notwithstanding, Shi Xie became General Who Pacifies the South over seven commanderies while retaining Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 」後燮遣吏張旻奉貢詣京都，是時天下喪亂，道路斷絕，而燮不廢貢職，特復下詔拜安遠將軍，封龍度亭侯。

translations.literal: Later Xie dispatched clerk Zhang Min to present tribute at the capital; at that time the realm was ruined and roads severed—yet Xie did not neglect tribute duty—the court specially issued an edict appointing him General Who Pacifies the Far and enfeoffing him Marquis of Longdu ting.
translations.idiomatic: Though highways were cut by war, Shi Xie still sent Zhang Min with tribute; the throne rewarded him as General Who Pacifies the Far and marquis of Longdu hamlet.

sentences.zh: 後巨與恭相失，舉兵逐恭，恭走還零陵。

translations.literal: Later Ju and Gong fell out with each other; Ju raised troops and expelled Gong—Gong fled back to Lingling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ju and Lai Gong quarreled; Wu Ju drove Lai Gong back to Lingling at spear-point.

sentences.zh: 建安十五年，孫權遣步騭為交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Jian'an Sun Quan dispatched Bu Zhi as Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 210 Sun Quan sent Bu Zhi south as inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 騭到，燮率兄弟奉承節度。

translations.literal: When Zhi arrived, Xie led his brothers in obeying his commands.
translations.idiomatic: Bu Zhi landed to find Shi Xie and his brothers ready to obey.

sentences.zh: 而吳巨懷異心，騭斬之。

translations.literal: But Wu Ju harbored a different intent—Zhi executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ju plotted rebellion—Bu Zhi executed him.

sentences.zh: 權加燮為左將軍。

translations.literal: Quan added Xie as General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named Shi Xie General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 建安末年，燮遣子廞入質，權以為武昌太守，燮、壹諸子在南者，皆拜中郎將。

translations.literal: Toward the end of Jian'an Xie sent his son Yin as hostage; Quan appointed Yin Grand Administrator of Wuchang—the sons of Xie and Yi who remained in the south were all appointed Gentlemen Generals.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Jian'an Shi Xie sent his son Yin as hostage; Sun Quan made Yin grand administrator of Wuchang and commissioned every Shi son still in the south as a gentleman-general.

sentences.zh: 燮又誘導益州豪姓雍闓等，率郡人民使遙東附，權益嘉之，遷衛將軍，封龍編侯，弟壹偏將軍，都鄉侯。

translations.literal: Xie also enticed powerful magnates of Yizhou such as Yong Kai, leading the people of the commandery to attach themselves distantly to the east—Quan prized him still more, promoted him to Guard General, enfeoffed him Marquis of Longbian—Yi became Lieutenant General and Marquis of Douxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie also lured Yizhou magnates like Yong Kai into Sun Quan's orbit; Sun Quan raised him to Guard General and marquis of Longbian while Shi Yi became lieutenant general and marquis of Douxiang township.

sentences.zh: 燮每遣使詣權，致雜香細葛，輒以千數，明珠、大貝、流離、翡翠、玳瑁、犀、象之珍，奇物異果，蕉、邪、龍眼之屬，無歲不至。

translations.literal: Whenever Xie sent envoys to Quan he delivered mixed incense and fine kudzu cloth—always by the thousand—bright pearls, great shells, liuli, kingfisher feathers, tortoise shell, rhinoceros horn, ivory—curious objects and exotic fruits—plantains, betel nuts, longyan—and the like—none failed to arrive year by year.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year his embassies bore incense, gauze, pearls, shells, glass, jade, tortoise shell, horn, ivory, and tropical fruit by the thousand-piece load.

sentences.zh: 壹時貢馬凡數百匹。

translations.literal: Yi at times presented tribute horses numbering several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi sometimes sent hundreds of horses.

sentences.zh: 權輒為書，厚加寵賜，以答慰之。

translations.literal: Quan always composed letters, lavishly granting favor and gifts to answer and console them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan answered each mission with letters and rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 燮在郡四十餘歲，黃武五年，年九十卒。

translations.literal: Xie was in the commandery over forty years; in the fifth year of Huangwu, aged ninety, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie ruled forty years and died at ninety in Huangwu 226.

sentences.zh: 權以交阯縣遠，乃分合浦以北為廣州，呂岱為刺史；

translations.literal: Quan, because Jiaozhi county was distant, therefore divided the territory north of Hepu to form Guangzhou—Lu Dai as Inspector;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan split the northern Gulf region into Guangzhou under Lu Dai—

sentences.zh: 交阯以南為交州，戴良為刺史。

translations.literal: south of Jiaozhi became Jiaozhou—Dai Liang as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: —and everything south of Jiaozhi into Jiaozhou under Dai Liang.

sentences.zh: 又遣陳時代燮為交阯太守。

translations.literal: He also dispatched Chen Shi to replace Xie as Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: He named Chen Shi to replace Shi Xie at Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 岱留南海，良與時俱前行到合浦，而燮子徽自署交阯太守，發宗兵拒良。

translations.literal: Dai remained at Nanhai—Liang and Shi advanced together and reached Hepu—but Xie's son Hui had styled himself Grand Administrator of Jiaozhi and raised lineage troops to resist Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dai stayed at Nanhai while Dai Liang and Chen Shi moved up—but Shi Hui had proclaimed himself grand administrator and mobilized clan levies against Dai Liang.

sentences.zh: 良留合浦。

translations.literal: Liang stayed at Hepu.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Liang halted at Hepu.

sentences.zh: 交阯桓鄰，燮舉吏也，叩頭諫徽使迎良，徽怒，笞殺鄰。

translations.literal: Huan Lin of Jiaozhi was an official whom Xie had promoted; he knocked his head in remonstration urging Hui to welcome Liang—Hui grew angry and had him flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Lin—once Shi Xie's clerk—begged Shi Hui to admit Dai Liang; Hui flew into a rage and beat him to death.

sentences.zh: 鄰兄治子發又合宗兵擊徽，徽閉門城守，治等攻之數月不能下，乃約和親，各罷兵還。

translations.literal: Lin's elder brother Zhi's son Fa again combined lineage troops to strike Hui; Hui shut the gates and defended the city—Zhi and the others attacked for months without taking it—thereupon they arranged peace by marriage and each withdrew their troops and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's son Fa rallied clan levies against Shi Hui, who barred the gates. Months of siege failed; the sides married into peace and stood down.

sentences.zh: 而呂岱被詔誅徽，自廣州將兵晝夜馳入，過合浦，與良俱前。

translations.literal: Lu Dai received an edict ordering him to execute Hui—from Guangzhou he led troops galloping day and night, passed Hepu, and advanced together with Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to kill Shi Hui, Lu Dai raced north from Guangzhou day and night, crossed Hepu, and joined Dai Liang.

sentences.zh: 壹子中郎將匡與岱有舊，岱署匡師友從事，先移書交阯，告喻禍福，又遣匡見徽，說令服罪，雖失郡守，保無他憂。

translations.literal: Yi's son Gentleman-General Kuang had old ties with Dai; Dai appointed Kuang Retainer for Mentor and Friend—first he sent a letter to Jiaozhi explaining fortune and disaster—also he dispatched Kuang to see Hui and persuade him to confess guilt—though he might lose the grand administrator position, he would be kept safe from other worries.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi's son Kuang, an old friend of Lu Dai, served as his liaison: Lu Dai wrote Jiaozhi warning of consequences and sent Kuang to urge Shi Hui to surrender—promising safety even at the cost of his office.

sentences.zh: 岱尋匡後至，徽兄祗，弟幹、頌等六人肉袒奉迎。

translations.literal: Dai arrived soon after Kuang—Hui's elder brother Zhi and younger brothers Gan, Song, and six others in all came bare-chested to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dai followed Kuang's arrival; Shi Hui's brothers Zhi, Gan, Song, and six more met him stripped to the waist in submission.

sentences.zh: 岱謝令復服，前至郡下。

translations.literal: Dai thanked them and ordered them to clothe themselves again, then advanced to below the commandery wall.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dai had them dress and marched to the city.

sentences.zh: 明旦早施帳幔，請徽兄弟以次入，賓客滿坐。

translations.literal: The next morning early they spread curtains and tents, inviting Hui's brothers to enter in order—guests filled the seats.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he pitched tents and seated a full hall when Shi Hui's brothers entered in turn.

sentences.zh: 岱起，擁節讀詔書，數徵罪過，左右因反縛以出，即皆伏誅，傳首詣武昌。

translations.literal: Dai rose, embraced the insignia, and read the edict, enumerating Hui's crimes—the attendants thereupon bound them hand behind back and led them out—all were executed on the spot; their heads were sent to Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Dai stood with his credentials, read the indictment, and had the Shi kin bound and beheaded; their heads went to Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 〈孙盛曰：夫柔远能迩，莫善於信；

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: To soften the distant and treat well the near—nothing excels trust;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observes: winning distant peoples and kin neighbors alike rests above all on good faith.

sentences.zh: 保大定功，莫善於义。

translations.literal: To preserve greatness and settle achievements—nothing excels righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Securing power and lasting deeds demands righteousness before all else.

sentences.zh: 故齐桓创基，德彰於柯会；

translations.literal: Therefore Duke Huan of Qi founded his enterprise—virtue shone at the meeting at Ke;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Duke Huan of Qi built Qi's throne—his virtue blazed at the Ke covenant.

sentences.zh: 晋文始伯，义显於伐原。

translations.literal: Duke Wen of Jin first became hegemon—righteousness appeared in the campaign against Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Wen of Jin first claimed hegemony—his justice showed in the attack on Yuan.

sentences.zh: 故能九合一匡，世主夏盟，令问长世，贻范百王。

translations.literal: Therefore they could nine times unite the lords and once rescue the royal house—the age's sovereigns presided at the summer assemblies—fine reputation lasting generations—bequeathing a model to a hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Hence their nine alliances and one restoration of the Zhou—lords who led the covenant leagues and left an enduring name for every throne that followed.

sentences.zh: 吕岱师友士匡，使通信誓，徽兄弟肉袒，推心委命，岱因灭之，以要功利，君子是以知孙权之不能远略，而吕氏之祚不延者也。〉

translations.literal: Lu Dai treated Shi Kuang as mentor and friend and sent pledges of communication—Hui's brothers bared their breasts and entrusted their lives—Dai thereupon annihilated them to pursue merit and profit—gentlemen therefore know that Sun Quan could not plan at long range, and the House of Lu's fortune would not extend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lu Dai played mentor to Shi Kuang, exchanged oaths, then slaughtered the Shi brothers who had come bare-skinned in surrender—profit over honor—by which men see Sun Quan's shortsighted southward policy and why the Lu line would not endure.

sentences.zh: 壹、䵋、匡後出，權原其罪，及燮質子廞，皆免為庶人。

translations.literal: Yi, Wei, and Kuang later emerged (to surrender); Quan forgave their crimes—together with Xie's hostage Yin—all were stripped to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yi, Wei, and Kuang later submitted and were pardoned along with hostage Shi Yin—yet all were reduced to commoners.

sentences.zh: 數歲，壹、䵋坐法誅。

translations.literal: Several years later Yi and Wei were executed for violating the law.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years Shi Yi and Wei died under sentence of law.

sentences.zh: 廞病卒，無子，妻寡居，詔在所月給俸米，賜錢四十萬。

translations.literal: Yin died of illness without sons; his wife lived as a widow—an edict ordered the local authorities to supply monthly salary grain and granted forty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yin died childless; his widow drew an imperial stipend of grain each month plus forty thousand cash.

translations.literal: 【Appraisal】
translations.idiomatic: Appraisal

sentences.zh: 評曰：劉繇藻厲名行，好尚臧否。

translations.literal: The appraisal states: Liu Yao polished his reputation and conduct and delighted in praising or blaming others.
translations.idiomatic: The historian judges Liu Yao a man who burnished his name and loved to praise or condemn his peers.

sentences.zh: 至於擾攘之時，據萬里之士，非其長也。

translations.literal: As for times of turmoil, holding territory ten thousand li across—this was not his forte.
translations.idiomatic: In chaos, commanding a realm measured in ten thousand li lay beyond his strength.

sentences.zh: 太史慈信義篤烈，有古人之分。

translations.literal: Taishi Ci's trustworthiness and duty were profound and fierce—he had the stature of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Taishi Ci embodied fierce loyalty worthy of classical exemplars.

sentences.zh: 士燮作守南越，優遊終世，至子不慎，自貽兇咎。

translations.literal: Shi Xie kept guard over Southern Yue at leisure his whole life—to his sons' lack of caution they brought catastrophe on themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xie ruled the deep south in ease for a lifetime; his sons' recklessness invited ruin.

sentences.zh: 蓋庸才玩富貴而恃阻險，使之然也。

translations.literal: This is how mediocre talent toys with wealth and nobility while trusting rugged barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Mediocre men cling to riches and rugged terrain—and come to grief.
